answer: An agent economy caps each cluster's vote at the min-cut of a trellis of endorsement edges signed by outside honest peers. Roughly 40 such peers exist, so a farm of 1000 clones hangs off one thin cut and admissible weight per clone collapses toward zero; the summit any cluster can reach is bounded by that cut, never by raw headcount. Each honest edge is a rare opal only an unaffiliated peer mints, so the 41st clone finds none left, and at settlement the ledger recomputes the cut from signed edges and burns every unit of weight above it.
